headings.title: Backup export, staged import and recovery flows

html:
Backup export, staged import and recovery flows

A backup has several owners: the Settings draft, a server export job, the browser's download manager, an import preview token and the offline startup owner. A successful step in one owner does not imply that later steps have completed. The Export / Import manual defines contents, exclusions, credentials, limits and operator commands. This guide traces the implementation boundaries and their failure behavior.

Ownership and exported data

flowchart TD Settings[Settings edits] --> Save[Pre-export save callback] Save --> Browser[Browser export controller] Browser --> Routes[Settings data routes] Routes --> Job[App-owned export job] Job --> Writer[Portable backup writer] Writer --> RAM[Complete immutable Controller revision] RAM --> Temp[Private per-domain materialization] Temp --> JSON[Private JSON output] Files[Separately inventoried managed files] --> JSON JSON --> Ready[Ready after writer and cancellation checks] Ready --> Response[Reader-pinned download response] Response --> Blob[Complete browser response chunks and Blob] Blob --> Download[Browser download manager]

data_transfer.js keeps one panel across Settings rerenders, updating its pre-export callback and reading staging status when remounted. export_progress.js owns the active export, polling, transfer and departure guards. Data-transfer routes create one ExportJobs manager for the application and expose its explicit commands and observations.

The Settings callback waits up to 100 intervals of 100 milliseconds for an existing save, calls saveNow(), and rejects export while saving or dirty keys remain. The export job starts only after that callback succeeds. This checks Settings-save completion; it does not wait for a new Controller disk checkpoint.

write_export resolves the active RAM owner when available. export_snapshot requires the full application inventory, captures one immutable domain revision and materializes it privately. Managed-file inventory and bytes are read separately; the domain snapshot is not a claim that arbitrary external files share an atomic filesystem revision. The portable encoder includes checksums and snapshot identity. Standalone export retains its existing database-reading path. The running Server continues to use RAM roots, without publishing a checkpoint for this export.

Jobs run serially: admission rejects another unsettled export or shutdown. A ready job may coexist with a later active job. Output directories/files are private, and job identities/files do not survive a server restart. Initial worker setup removes leftover private job directories. Timing history is bounded supporting metadata; failure to save that history does not fail a completed backup.

Creation, observation and download

sequenceDiagram actor U as Human participant B as Export controller participant S as Settings save callback participant A as Export API participant J as Export worker participant D as Download manager U->>B: Export JSON B->>S: Finish current Settings save S-->>B: Saved or rejected opt Save succeeded B->>A: POST exports with independently observable response A->>J: Admit serialized job A-->>B: Accepted job ID and state loop Until ready or terminal failure B->>B: Wait one second B->>A: GET job status A->>J: Renew heartbeat and read status A-->>B: Stage, state and estimate end alt Ready B->>A: GET ready download A->>J: Acquire file reader reference A-->>B: Stream complete JSON response A->>J: Release reader in response finally B->>B: Check abort and declared response length B->>D: Hand off JSON Blob and filename B-->>U: JSON ready, download started else Terminal or repeated transport failure B->>A: Best-effort cancellation B-->>U: Report failure without a download end end

The browser has one active export per view. It polls at one-second intervals and tolerates two consecutive status-read failures, showing reconnecting status. A third failure ends observation and requests cancellation. A successful read resets that failure counter. It does not automatically retry job creation. The worker cooperatively cancels an unsettled job after more than 300 seconds without heartbeat; settled jobs without readers expire after 600 seconds. These checks run when the worker reaps, rather than promising exact wall-clock cleanup deadlines.

Each local one-second paint ages the last estimate without making a request. Observations older than five seconds show Re-estimating…. The live region changes when the stage sentence changes; timer ticks update the separate time presentation. Download ETA uses measured byte-rate samples, at least three samples and two elapsed seconds, and requires a declared content length. It remains an estimate, not a completion signal.

The browser accumulates chunks, releases the stream reader, checks cancellation and checks received length when a nonzero Content-Length was supplied. It then creates a JSON Blob URL, clicks a download link and schedules URL revocation after 60 seconds. Download started confirms this handoff; it does not confirm a filesystem save, user-selected destination or free disk capacity. The browser does not write streamed chunks directly to disk.

The server response holds a reader reference through its finally block, including stream errors/disconnects. Cancellation and expiry defer private-file cleanup while readers still hold it. Export-worker cancellation is checked before ready publication and again during settlement, so a racing cancellation can win over a just-finished write. Shutdown requests cancellation and joins the worker before releasing ownership.

Departure and creation races

sequenceDiagram actor U as Human participant B as Browser export owner participant A as Export API participant J as Server job B->>A: POST create without browser abort signal par Creation response still pending A->>J: Accept job A-->>B: Job identity and Human confirms departure or page hides U->>B: Leave page B->>B: Mark leaving and abort owned observation opt Job identity already known B->>A: Best-effort keepalive cancellation A->>J: Request cooperative cancellation end end opt Creation returns after local abort B->>A: Cancel the newly learned identity A->>J: Request cooperative cancellation end Note over B,J: Navigation does not wait for cancellation acknowledgement

Ordinary same-tab HTTP(S) links show a Stay/Cancel confirmation. Modified clicks, download links, other browsing targets and same-page fragments are not intercepted. Reload/close uses the browser's native warning; dismissing it leaves the export running. Confirmed navigation and pagehide request best-effort cancellation and abort local reads/delays. The independent creation request allows a late identity to be cancelled if its response still reaches the page. It cannot guarantee that a departed browser will receive that response; heartbeat expiry remains a server cleanup mechanism. Repeated cancellation requests are possible.

Import preview, staging and cancellation

sequenceDiagram actor U as Human participant P as Settings panel participant A as Data-transfer routes participant L as Staging lifecycle U->>P: Choose JSON file P->>P: Clear old preview and check 512 MiB limit P->>A: POST preview with raw JSON bytes A->>A: Check supplied origin, media type and streamed size A->>L: Validate in isolated temporary storage L-->>P: Current token, version and record/file counts U->>P: Acknowledge replacement and confirm P->>A: POST import with token and replace_existing true A->>L: Require current token and no pending import L->>L: Rename preview.json to pending.json and sync L-->>P: Restart-required staged state Note over P,L: Running repositories are unchanged opt Human cancels before restart U->>P: Cancel pending import P->>A: DELETE import A->>L: Remove cancellable preview/pending metadata L-->>P: Current staging status end

The panel serializes its actions. A staged import disables another upload while leaving export available. Preview summaries render as literal text, and confirm requires both the current token and the replacement acknowledgement. The server independently enforces those conditions. Preview does not replace live application records, although it writes private preview metadata containing the validated backup. A newer successful preview replaces the earlier token; stale confirmation conflicts.

lifecycle.py owns locked preview/staging metadata and atomic JSON writes. HTTP preview and confirm perform blocking work in the threadpool. Supplied origins must match the request host; JSON uploads also pass media-type and streamed-size checks. These route checks supplement the application's authentication/CSRF boundary. Expected export conflicts map to 409 and missing jobs to 404; import confirmation/cancellation errors use 409.

Mount/remount performs a quiet staging-status read, not a polling subscription. The panel adopts a positive pending result; an empty result does not comprehensively reset prior local pending state after cancellation in another browser. A read or write error is shown without assuming that an earlier accepted staging operation rolled back. The server remains authoritative across reloads and multiple clients.

Offline installation and commit recovery

flowchart TD Owner[Exclusive offline bootstrap owner] --> Journal{Generation journal exists?} Journal -->|Yes| Commit{Manifest names its generation?} Commit -->|Yes| Verify[Verify committed generation] Commit -->|No| Rollback[Restore previous managed files] Journal -->|No| Legacy[Resolve legacy journal if present] Legacy --> Pending{Pending import exists?} Pending -->|No| Return[Current or later normal bootstrap] Pending -->|Yes| Validate[Revalidate in temporary storage] Validate -->|Valid| Space[Preflight additional disk copies] Validate -->|Rejected| Reject[Retain current generation and reject staging] Reject --> Return Space -->|Insufficient| Capacity[Fail startup with pending intent retained] Space -->|Sufficient| Build[Build and verify complete new generation] Build --> Originals[Copy managed originals and publish journal] Originals --> Install[Install incoming managed files] Install --> Publish[Atomically publish new manifest] Install -. Failure after journaling .-> Commit Publish -. Failure after journaling .-> Commit Publish --> Verify Verify --> Retire[Remove pending and journal, retire temporary history] Rollback --> Retire Retire --> Return

The Server's bootstrap lifecycle resolves pending runtime purge work, then calls generation_import.apply_pending before installing repositories or starting workers. Import requires the current process's exclusive owner, BOOTSTRAPPING phase and no installed domains. It revalidates with the code actually starting, so an upgrade after preview can still reject the backup. A validation rejection retains the existing generation and moves staging to rejected.json. Insufficient disk preflight leaves pending intent for a later retry; preflight is a capacity estimate, not a reservation.

New domain files, managed-file retention and logical recovery metadata are built and verified before publication. Current canonical database paths are not overwritten by this protocol. Before replacing managed files, the importer copies their originals and durably publishes a journal containing their paths and the target generation. The atomic checkpoints/manifest.json replacement commits the imported generation. An error before publication restores the previous managed files; an error after publication verifies the committed generation rather than undoing it. Restart uses the same journal/manifest decision. Recovery inside an I/O exception handler re-raises the original exception after resolving storage, so that startup attempt still fails and normal bootstrap resumes on a later attempt. A journal published just before interruption remains for the next owner to resolve.

Recovery rejects changed destination paths or hub identity and validates a committed generation before retiring recovery state. Once resolved, it removes pending intent and the journal, retires superseded generations and removes temporary original copies. The Settings panel's recovery-copy wording describes that temporary protection; it is not a promise of a permanently retained previous backup. See Controller persistence for the authoritative checkpoint, logical recovery and mirror contracts.

A retained legacy journal.json is handled by the canonical-file installer in lifecycle.apply_pending, before a new generation import proceeds. That older protocol copies original databases/managed folders, journals replacement, runs preflight and marks commit. Its rollback must match the original destination paths. The two journal formats have distinct commit rules and are not interchangeable.

Review boundary

The two browser modules, HTTP route module, staging lifecycle, generation importer, export-job owner and RAM export adapter were read in full. Settings-save wiring, Server startup and the portable encoder were inspected only at the linked boundaries; backup schema compatibility retains its existing service/manual evidence. Tests use isolated local data, fake response streams and injected storage failures. No live installation, release, model workload or user-data restore is performed. Appearance and tooltip implementation remain outside this pass.
